q: The theory of coalgebraic modal logic provides a syntax for specifying properties of coalgebras (dynamical systems). Bisimulation between two coalgebras (X,α) and (Y,β) for functor F is a relation R ⊆ X × Y such that:
opts: R is an F-coalgebra morphism in the span: (R, F-rel(α,β): R → F(R)) where F-rel lifts R to F(R)
exp: Bisimulation for F-coalgebras: R is a bisimulation if there is a coalgebra structure on R making both projections π₁: R → X and π₂: R → Y into coalgebra morphisms. For transition systems (F = P, the powerset functor), this recovers the classical Park-Milner bisimulation.
